diagnostic_evidence.quote: Unlike HOSVD, sequentially truncated HOSVD (ST-HOSVD) performs the truncation sequentially across modes by projecting the tensor onto lower-dimensional subspaces one mode at a time.

issues.failure_explanation: Every factor is computed from the unchanged original unfolding, rather than from the current compressed core. Thus the executable algorithm is HOSVD with sequential core formation, not ST-HOSVD. In particular, its later SVDs do not benefit from the progressively reduced dimensions assumed in the ST-HOSVD cost comparison.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the leading left singular vectors of the current core unfolding G_(i) before performing each core update.
issues.overall_effect: The deterministic ST-HOSVD procedure and its claimed computational distinction from HOSVD are not implemented as stated.
issues.title: The stated ST-HOSVD algorithm computes factors from the original tensor
issues.why_classification: This is a local change to one executable step, using the current core already maintained by the algorithm; no new method or analysis is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: are independent random matrices whose entries are mean zero, unit variance,  subgaussian random variables, with subgaussian norm  bounded by $K \geq 1$.
where $\{\V{\omega}_j\}_{j=1}^d$ are independent, and have independent entries with zero mean and unit variance.

issues.failure_explanation: Independence of the factor matrices does not imply independence of entries within a factor or independence of its columns. For example, take each factor to be an all-ones matrix multiplied by one Rademacher variable, independently across factors. This satisfies the definition, but all KRP columns coincide and their covariance is the all-ones matrix, not the identity. The proof introduces an additional independence premise.

failure_location.quote: The random matrix has independent and isotropic columns, i.e., $\expect[\V{\Omega}(:,k)] = \V{0}$ and $\expect[\V{\Omega}(:,k)\V{\Omega}(:,k)\t]  = \M{I}_{N}$ for $1 \leq k \leq \ell$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly require mutual independence of the entries within each factor matrix, in addition to independence among factors, as already assumed in the proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The isotropy, independent-sample concentration, and subsequent guarantees do not hold for the full class admitted by Definition def:subgauss.
issues.title: The KRP definition does not supply the entrywise independence used throughout
issues.why_classification: Making this standard sampling hypothesis explicit is a local repair that preserves the independent-entry sketching methods, distribution choices, and rates analyzed in the paper.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Without any loss of generality, assume that $\M{V}$ is nonzero.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement allows V=0. Then its event is {0≥0}, with probability one, whereas the right side is less than one for t>C_{K,d}(ln 2)^d. Consequently, excluding V=0 in the proof is not without loss of generality for the stated non-strict tail event.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma for nonzero V and handle V=0 directly wherever needed, or formulate the tail event with a strict inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The tail lemma fails in an explicitly permitted degenerate case; the downstream zero-matrix norm bounds themselves are trivial.
issues.title: The one-column tail lemma is false for the zero matrix
issues.why_classification: A routine boundary-case correction preserves the substantive concentration and approximation guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: Conditional Chernoff requires the conditional mean E[Y|E], not the unconditional mean ℓI. The event factors over columns, so independence can survive, but isotropy generally does not. Already for a scalar Gaussian projection, conditioning every squared entry to be at most a finite cutoff reduces its mean below one. The analogous conditional application in Step 2 has the same unaddressed change of mean.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use independent zero-truncated summands and bound the lost covariance by integrating the available column-norm tail bound. A larger cutoff, such as one with a doubled logarithm, supplies room to control this bias; rerun Chernoff with the truncated mean and propagate the resulting safety constants through the dependent results.
issues.overall_effect: The principal singular-value concentration argument, and hence the range-finding, tensor-compression, single-view, and subspace-embedding proofs, are not established as written.
issues.title: Conditioning on bounded column norms changes the mean used in matrix Chernoff
issues.why_classification: The supplied tail estimates support a contained truncation-and-bias argument with comparable asymptotic bounds, but a nontrivial additional lemma and revised constants are required.

issues.failure_explanation: The required equation is ε²/(2+ε)=Γ, whose positive root is (Γ+sqrt(Γ²+8Γ))/2. Substituting ε=2Γ meets the required inequality only when Γ≥1. No such lower bound is assumed; rank-one Z and sufficiently large ℓ allow Γ to approach zero. Thus the asserted upper-tail estimate does not follow even if the conditioning problem is independently repaired.

issues.overall_effect: The small-Gamma upper-tail estimate and the approximation-error factors obtained from it are unsupported.
